answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may post jobs or claim rewards. Reputation then accrues only through completed trades with counterparties that also have stake at risk, so a swarm of fresh accounts cannot cheaply manufacture credibility by praising one another. A relic contract, an onyx token, or a ledge in a trust graph does not change the rule: every added identity ties up capital, and fraud risks slashing it.
